stemMd: A museum replaced some object labels with questions inviting visitors to compare nearby exhibits. Visitors subsequently spent longer in those rooms, although the museum did not test what they remembered. Which conclusion is supported?

options.label: A
options.textMd: All visitors disliked the new labels.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The change was associated with longer visits, but its effect on retention was not measured.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The museum proved that memory cannot be tested.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Visitors necessarily learned twice as much.

explanationMd: The evidence concerns duration, while retention remains unmeasured. Keep the conclusion within the variable actually observed and avoid turning an association into proof of an educational effect.

distractorRationale.e: Time spent does not quantify learning.
distractorRationale.d: It merely did not test memory.
